ITEM.PTXT: A wireless remote control system has been adopted, enabling remote locking/unlocking of all doors with the electronic key.
An encrypted code has been adopted for the weak radio waves (identification code) used between the electronic key and the door control receiver for improved security.
A customize function using the diagnostic tool (TaSCAN) enables adjustment and setting of various functions.

INDICATE.TITLE: List of Wireless Remote Control Main Functions

ENTRY.PTXT: Pressing the lock/unlock button locks/unlocks all doors.

After the Certification ECU receives the encrypted code transmitted from the electronic key via the door control receiver, it verifies the code, and when it recognizes the code as that of its own vehicle, door unlocking, etc. becomes possible.
If the doors are left unlocked for approximately 30 seconds after being unlocked by pressing the unlock button, all doors are locked automatically to prevent the vehicle from being left unlocked.
If the lock button is pressed to lock the doors while any door is ajar or open, the wireless answer-back buzzer sounds for approximately 10 seconds to warn that a door has not been closed.
When the doors are locked/unlocked using the wireless remote control, the wireless answer-back buzzer sounds and the hazard warning lights flash 1 time(s) when locking and 2 time(s) when unlocking.
When the doors are unlocked by the wireless remote control with the room light switch in the "DOOR" position, the room light, etc. illuminates for approximately 15 seconds.

ITEM.PTXT: If any door is opened or all doors are locked within 30 seconds, the 30-second auto lock function is cancelled.

The buzzer stops sounding when the power is turned ON (ACC/IG ON), all doors are closed, the door lock control switch (key-linked) is operated, or the doors are unlocked by the wireless/smart unlock function.
The answer-back function also operates when locking is performed by the 30-second auto lock function.

INDICATE.TITLE: Wireless Remote Control System Wiring Diagram

ITEM.PTXT: When the lock button 〈unlock button〉 is pressed, the vehicle identification code and function code are transmitted by weak radio waves. When the door control receiver receives these, it sends them to the Certification ECU.

The Certification ECU verifies the identification code and determines the function code; when it recognizes that the identification code matches that of its own vehicle and that the function code is door lock/〈unlock〉, it outputs this as code data to the Main Body ECU.

When the Main Body ECU receives the lock 〈unlock〉 signal, it turns ON the lock relay 〈unlock relay〉 and locks 〈unlocks〉 all doors, in the same way as manual lock 〈unlock〉 operation of the power door lock system.

When the Main Body ECU receives the door lock position switch OFF 〈ON〉 state signal from each door lock assembly and confirms lock 〈unlock〉, it performs answer-back output. For door unlock operation, if no door is opened (door courtesy light switch ON) for approximately 30 seconds, all doors are locked (auto lock control starts).
The electronic key has a lock button and unlock button, enabling the same operation as the wireless remote control system. A CR1632 battery is used.

A mechanical key and transponder (communication chip) are built in. When the electrical key battery is depleted, the doors can be locked/unlocked by inserting the mechanical key into the driver side door key cylinder, and the engine can be started by touching the electrical key to the front of the engine switch.
A relay device that receives radio waves of a certain frequency and sends them back on a different frequency.
The key is a precision device. Observe the following points.
Do not subject it to strong impacts
Do not leave it in hot places for long periods
Do not clean it with an ultrasonic cleaner, etc.
Do not use it together with magnetic key holders (magnets, etc.)
Do not attach stickers, etc. to the key surface

If a key is lost, promptly bring all remaining keys to the nearest dealer. If a lost key is left unattended, there are disadvantages such as an extremely high risk of theft and increased replacement costs when parts fail.
The standard key set includes 2 electronic keys.
Even if a button on the electronic key is held down, transmission of the weak radio waves stops after approximately 20 seconds.

By registering the transponder ID code, electronic key ID code and transmitter identification code in the verification ECU, the system can accommodate the use of multiple electronic keys, etc. (For the methods of adding, rewriting, checking and prohibiting identification codes, refer to the Repair Manual.)

The operation indicator light (LED) illuminates not only during button operation but also during communication (transmission) for ID verification, allowing the operating condition and battery depletion to be checked.
